title: Bar charts and line graphs
summary: Draw bar charts and line graphs from a table, read them, and choose the right chart for a question.
guide: This studio covers bar charts (Years 2–4), line graphs (Year 5) and choosing a suitable chart.
Charts are drawn left to right, with the value axis on the left going up.
To build a chart, drag a bar or point up and down with your finger, or use the arrow keys.
A bar chart compares several groups. A line graph shows how one thing changes over time. When the value axis does not start at 0, we draw a break mark on it.
Ask your child: "What does this chart tell us?"

engine.instruction-drag: Drag the bars or points up and down.

build-bar.title: Draw a bar chart
build-bar.prompt: The table shows how many books were borrowed from the class library each day. Predict which bar will be tallest. Then drag each bar up to the right number.
build-bar.hint: The axis goes up in 2s: 0, 2, 4, … 5 is half-way between 4 and 6.
build-bar.success: Well done! Tuesday, with 8 books, has the tallest bar and Wednesday, with 3, the shortest.
build-bar.why: Without reading the numbers, how can you tell from the chart which day had the most books borrowed?
build-bar.model: I look for the tallest bar. All bars start at 0 and are the same width, so a taller bar means more books. Tuesday has the tallest bar.

feedback.empty: Drag the bars up with your finger.
feedback.key-ignored: Your bars are twice as tall! Each line on the axis is 2, not 1. Read the numbers on the axis.
feedback.too-high: One bar is taller than its number. Check it against the table.
feedback.too-low: One bar is shorter than its number. Check it against the table.

read-bar.title: Read a bar chart
read-bar.prompt: This chart shows how many pages each child read in a week. How many more pages did Maryam read than Sara?
read-bar.hint: The top of Sara's bar is between 6 and 8; Maryam's is between 14 and 16. Read each one exactly, then subtract.
read-bar.success: Right! Maryam read 15 pages and Sara 7: 15 − 7 = 8.
read-bar.why: Sara's bar stops between two lines. How did you know it was 7?
read-bar.model: The lines go up in 2s: 6 and 8. Sara's bar stops exactly half-way between them, and half-way between 6 and 8 is 7. In the same way Maryam's bar is half-way between 14 and 16, so 15.

feedback.counted-steps: You counted the squares between the bars. But each square is 2 pages, not 1.
feedback.added: You added the two children's pages. "How many more" means subtract.
feedback.not-difference: That is all of Maryam's pages. We want to know how many more than Sara she read.
feedback.misread: You read Sara's bar as 6. Its top is half-way between 6 and 8.
feedback.too-big: Too big. Read the bars again: each line is 2 pages.
feedback.too-small: Too small. Read the bars again: each line is 2 pages.

build-line.title: Draw a line graph
build-line.prompt: Maryam measured a bean plant every week. Drag each week's point up to the right height. The line joins the points.
build-line.hint: Each line on the axis is 2 cm. 7 is half-way between 6 and 8.
build-line.success: Well done! The plant got taller every week: 2, 4, 7, 9 and 12 cm.
build-line.why: Looking at the line, in which week did the plant grow most? How can you tell?
build-line.model: Where the line is steepest. From week 2 to 3 it grew 3 cm, and from week 4 to 5 also 3 cm; the other weeks 2 cm. The steeper the line goes up, the more it grew.

feedback.empty: Drag the points up with your finger.
feedback.key-ignored: Your points are twice as high! Each line on the axis is 2 cm.
feedback.too-high: One point is higher than its number. Check it against the table.
feedback.too-low: One point is lower than its number. Check it against the table.

read-line.title: An axis that doesn't start at 0
read-line.prompt: This graph shows Sara's height from age 6 to age 10. The axis starts at 100. How tall was Sara at age 6, in centimetres?
read-line.hint: The break mark at the bottom of the axis means the numbers start at 100. The point for age 6 is between 110 and 120. Where exactly?
read-line.success: Right! The point is exactly half-way between 110 and 120: 115 cm.
read-line.why: Why does this graph's axis start at 100 instead of 0?
read-line.model: Because all the heights are between 110 and 140. Starting at 0 would leave most of the graph empty and make the changes look tiny. The break mark reminds us that the bottom of the axis is not 0.

feedback.axis-start: You took the bottom of the axis as 0. But the axis starts at 100! Look at the break mark.
feedback.grid-line: The point is not on a line; it is between two lines. What is half-way between 110 and 120?
feedback.too-big: Too big. Read the point for age 6 again.
feedback.too-small: Too small. Read the point for age 6 again.

choose-chart.title: Choose a chart
choose-chart.prompt: Reza measured the temperature in the school yard every two hours (in °C). He wants to show how the temperature changed during the day. Which chart is best?
choose-chart.hint: The temperature went up and down as the hours passed. Which chart shows change with a line?
choose-chart.success: Right! A line graph shows the temperature rising until 2 pm and then falling.
choose-chart.why: Why is a pie chart not suitable for this data?
choose-chart.model: A pie chart shows the parts of one whole, like how many children in a class like each fruit. Temperatures are not parts of a whole, and adding them up means nothing. We want change over time, which is what a line graph shows.

feedback.not-whole: A pie chart is for the parts of a whole. Do the temperatures make up a whole?
feedback.bar-change: A bar chart compares the temperatures, but a line shows change over time better.
feedback.picto-measure: Pictures are for counting things. Temperature is measured, not counted.
feedback.wrong-chart: Think again: the question is about change over time.
